source_evidence: Unlike traditional mutual funds (or “open-end funds”), they are not required to buy back shares from shareholders.
answer: A key difference is how shares are handled. Traditional open-end mutual funds are required to buy back shares from shareholders, while publicly traded closed-end funds are not. Closed-end fund shares are sold in a public offering and then trade on national securities exchanges at market prices, which can be above or below the market value of the fund’s underlying investments.
